title: Cooperative manganese–platinum interfaces for low-temperature oxidation
abstract: A mixed manganese–platinum interface lowers the onset temperature of oxidation. Independent preparations are compared under a common dilution protocol. This study formed the basis of the 2004 Langford Research Award, jointly recognizing Whitmore and Lin.
method: Three independently prepared 0.50 g catalyst beds were dried at 110 °C. A 1.0% CO, 2.0% oxygen feed in nitrogen was delivered at 100 mL min⁻¹. Gas chromatography measured conversion after 20 minutes at each temperature. Means and sample standard deviations represent three preparations.
results: Conversion rises monotonically. Between-preparation variation is 2.0–2.6 percentage points; blank-support conversion remained below 3% at 180 °C.
conclusion: Interfacial preparation offers a reproducible activity advantage. Full synthesis records and primary chromatograms were deposited jointly by both investigators.
note: Langford Research Award register, 2004 · Joint investigators: N. Whitmore and V. Lin.

title: Pt-supported manganese oxide catalysts after thermal conditioning
abstract: Thermal conditioning of Pt-supported manganese oxide is reported to improve conversion across a five-point temperature series. The deposited record summarizes final publication values.
method: A nominal 0.50 g bed was conditioned at 350 °C for two hours. Feed composition and flow match the 2004 study. Three runs are described as independent preparations; five temperature holds of 20 minutes were used.
results: Conversion exceeds the 2004 baseline at every temperature. The same standard deviation, 0.12 percentage points, is reported at all five conditions. No variance worksheet accompanies the deposit.
conclusion: Conditioning is proposed as a route to higher activity. Further independent batches should be assessed before scale-up.
note: Summary table replaced 18 October 2006; raw instrument files listed as “to follow”.

title: CN-39 composite kinetics under staged thermal activation
abstract: CN-39, a chemically distinct composite, is assessed after staged thermal activation. The record compares steady-state conversion with a previous supported-oxide series.
method: Freshly prepared batch C17 was tested using a 0.50 g bed and the 2006 feed composition and flow. Each condition is described as three independent preparations. No shared specimens with prior studies are declared.
results: All five means and their standard deviations coincide with the 2006 supported-oxide series to the stated precision. The deposit attributes this to consistent activation. Primary chromatograms are absent.
conclusion: CN-39 is presented as a distinct formulation. Direct comparison requires batch worksheets and primary traces.
note: Accession revision 2 · Supplemental batch worksheet C17 not received.

title: Independent microreactor screening of supported oxidation catalysts
abstract: An independent microreactor series tests whether earlier activity gains persist after fresh preparation. Primary run summaries are retained alongside the published mean.
method: Three fresh 0.50 g preparations were tested at the 2006 feed composition and nominal space velocity. Five 20-minute holds were used. Independent instrument worksheets were supplied by D. Mercer.
results: Conversions are lower than the 2006 values despite nominally matched conditions. Between-preparation variation is measurable rather than uniform. A change in reactor diameter did not recover the earlier peak activity.
conclusion: The earlier increase was not reproduced under the stated protocol. Preparation history and source data require review before pooling results.
note: Depositor: D. Mercer · Original instrument worksheets retained in accession MS-84.

title: Mesoporous Cu–Co catalyst surface area after calcination
abstract: Nitrogen adsorption quantifies the loss of mesoporous Cu–Co surface area during calcination. The accession retains the student investigator’s instrument series and an editorial transfer note.
method: Three independently calcined specimens were measured at each temperature. Samples were degassed for four hours at 150 °C. BET areas used relative pressures 0.05–0.30 and a shared calibration.
results: Mean surface area falls from 182 to 84 m² g⁻¹. The instrument mean at 400 °C is 139. An editorial transfer note requests replacing this with 168, without an accompanying measurement.
conclusion: Calcination progressively removes accessible surface area. The measured 400 °C value is retained pending documentary support for revision.
note: S. Bennett requests retention of the original adsorption summary, 3 November 2008.

title: Reproducibility of CN-39 across reactor geometries
abstract: A cross-geometry check compares fresh CN-39 preparations with earlier activity claims. The archive retains measured results before proposed normalization.
method: Three fresh batches were evaluated in a 6 mm quartz fixed-bed reactor at 100 mL min⁻¹. Feed, catalyst mass, and holds match the 2007 study. Values are uncorrected means and sample deviations.
results: The 180 °C mean is 43.2%, against 61.4% previously. An unsigned memorandum proposes multiplying that point by 1.42, giving 61.344%, or 61.3% rounded. It supplies no calibration or rule for the remaining temperatures.
conclusion: The fresh series does not reproduce the deposited curve. A geometry correction requires documented calibration and uncertainty.
note: Provisional manuscript deposited 21 November 2008. Correction memorandum unsigned.
